code_shape:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# M3 acceptance gates — run from the repo root: ./scripts/m3-acceptance-gates.sh
# Each gate states what it asserts and what a red result MEANS. Gates that are
# red today (G4, G4b, G5, G6) are red because the work is not done, not because
# the gate is wrong. Do not 'fix' a red gate by editing it.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

FAILED=0
fail() { printf '  DO   %-4s %s\n' "$1" "$2"; FAILED=$((FAILED + 1)); }
ok()   { printf '  XANH %-4s %s\n' "$1" "$2"; }

gate_eq() { # gate_eq <id> <expected> <actual> <what-it-means-when-red>
  if [ "$3" -eq "$2" ]; then ok "$1" "$3/$2"; else fail "$1" "$3 (muc $2) — $4"; fi
}

# --- G4: no raw wheel multiplier survives outside the shared module -----------
WHEEL=$( { grep -rn 'event\.wheel \* [0-9]' packages/tui/src --include='*.ts'
           grep -rn 'delta \* [0-9]'     packages/tui/src --include='*.ts'; } \
         | grep -v '^packages/tui/src/mouse-wheel\.ts:' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
gate_eq G4 0 "$WHEEL" "mot literal con lai; overlay ramp canh khong ramp"

# --- G4b: all nine sites import the shared module -----------------------------
WHEEL_FILES=( packages/tui/src/overlays/agent-transcript-viewer.ts
              packages/tui/src/overlays/plan-review-overlay.ts
              packages/tui/src/overlays/rewind-selector.ts
              packages/tui/src/apps/debug/log-viewer.ts
              packages/tui/src/overlays/usage-dashboard.ts
              packages/tui/src/overlays/copy-selector.ts
              packages/tui/src/apps/git/sidebar.ts
              packages/tui/src/apps/debug/raw-sse.ts
              packages/tui/src/apps/git/git-tui.ts )
missing=0
for f in "${WHEEL_FILES[@]}"; do grep -q 'mouse-wheel' "$f" || { missing=$((missing+1)); fail G4b "khong import: $f"; }; done
[ "$missing" -eq 0 ] && ok G4b "9/9"

# --- G5: read-group membership (plan lines 7504-7519, verbatim) ---------------
hits=$(grep -nE '[!=]== "read"' \
  packages/tui/src/chat/read-tool-group.ts \
  packages/tui/src/chat/chat-transcript-builder.ts \
  packages/coding-agent/src/modes/utils/ui-helpers.ts \
  packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/event-controller.ts)
left=$(printf '%s\n' "$hits" | grep -v 'event-controller\.ts:[0-9]*:.*event\.toolName === "read"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
kept=$(printf '%s\n' "$hits" | grep -c 'event\.toolName === "read"')
printf '%s\n' "$hits"   # in the remaining sites so a red gate names the culprit
if [ "$left" -eq 0 ] && [ "$kept" -eq 3 ]; then ok G5 "left=0 kept=3"
else fail G5 "membership con lai=$left (muc 0) | inline giu nguyen=$kept (muc 3)"; fi

# --- G10: no mock.module() calls (CALL form; the corpus documents the ban) ---
MM=$(grep -rnE 'mock\.module\(' packages/coding-agent/test packages/tui/test \
      | grep -vE '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(//|\*|/\*)' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
gate_eq G10 0 "$MM" "mock.module() global registry leak sang file khac"

# --- G12: no reference-tree contamination in shipped source -------------------
CONTAM=$(grep -rn 'claude-code-best' packages/ scripts/ docs/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
gate_eq G12 0 "$CONTAM" "van con tham chieu cay dich nguoc trong ma ship"

# --- G1,G2,G3,G6,G7,G8,G9,G11: file exists AND passes ------------------------
gate_test() { # gate_test <id> <test-path> <which-wave>
  if [ ! -f "$2" ]; then fail "$1" "thieu $2 — can $3"
  elif bun test "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "$1" "$2"
  else fail "$1" "FAIL $2 — xem contract cua $3"; fi
}

exit $(( FAILED > 0 ))
test_contract:
THIS ITEM SHIPS NO NEW *.test.ts, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME — the reasoning is a finding, not a shortcut.

(1) The gates in §7.1 are source greps. AGENTS.md bans source-grep from tests outright: 'A test that reads an implementation file (.ts/.rs/build script) and asserts on its text — expect(src).toContain("someCall()") ... is banned. It tests how code _looks_, not what it _does_.' G4, G4b, G5 and G10 are literally `grep -rn` counts. Putting them in a `*.test.ts` would be the exact banned shape. The plan already half-sees this — its G5 note says the grep 'bổ sung cho' (complements) the behavioural test rather than replacing it. So the grep half belongs in a shell script a reviewer runs, and the behavioural half belongs in the per-wave test files the sibling specs already specify. Neither belongs in a new file authored here.

(2) The one real testable legal contract tail1 could own is already owned. `scripts/ci-release-publish.ts:100` exports `legalPayloadFiles(license)` and it THROWS on a missing license — `scripts/ci-release-publish.test.ts:143-146` asserts `expect(() => legalPayloadFiles(undefined)).toThrow('Unsupported package license: <missing>')`. So 'every published package declares a licence' is already enforced at publish time and already tested. AGENTS.md: 'Don't duplicate coverage across abstraction levels. If an integration test already proves the behavior, drop the narrower unit test that restates it.' Adding a package-licence test here would be a duplicate that can only rot.

(3) What the consumer actually sees if this regresses: the reviewer's gate run stops being trustworthy. The failure mode is not a crash — it is a green gate that means nothing, or a red gate on a correct tree that teaches the team to wave gates through. Both are silent. G10 as the plan literally writes it is already in that second state today (2 hits, both comments), which is why step 5 corrects it before anything is written.

The defensible artifact is therefore the SCRIPT plus its exit code, and the gate below is measured, not asserted.

gate_can_fail:
Yes, three independent ways, all measured on this tree rather than reasoned about.

FIRST: the gates are red before the work. G4 = 9 (needs 0), G4b = 0/9 (needs 9/9), G5 left = 7 (needs 0), G6 file absent. If someone lands the script and the gates come out green on Monday morning, the gates are broken — that is the failure this gate is designed to catch, and it is the same pathology the plan diagnoses in G4's own rewrite note ('the old gate self-adjusted and could not distinguish A3 done from A3 not done').

SECOND: G10 catches its own historical bug. The plan's literal form returns 2 on a completely correct tree, because two test files contain comments explaining they do NOT use mock.module. A reviewer would either patch the gate or wave it through. The corrected form returns 0.

THIRD: a stale anchor is caught. The plan's seven `* 3` line numbers are ALL wrong (off by +1 to +13). A script transcribed from the plan prose instead of the tree would grep nine files at nine wrong lines; if a future edit shifts them, the file-existence half still passes while the intent is silently lost. Step 4 forbids transcribing from prose for exactly this reason.

What this gate does NOT do: it does not prove UI fidelity. §7.2 says so in the plan's own words — 'phần này không thể chứng minh bằng máy' — and that half stays human. A reviewer reading XANH on all eleven gates has learned nothing about whether the wheel ramp feels right on Ghostty, and the doc must say so where §7.2's four human judgements live.

§8.6 #5 (write the clean-room policy down) is blocked on step 1's human answer, and until it is answered nothing stops a future contributor from copying from a reverse-engineered tree — CONTRIBUTING.md:82-91 requires 'the right to submit' but names no specific hazard, which is the gap §8.6 #5 identifies.
Nothing upstream. tail1 consumes the waves; no wave waits on it.
effort: S — roughly half a day. One shell script (~120 lines including the eight test-gate stubs), one markdown doc (~150 lines), an optional eight-line CONTRIBUTING addendum. No runtime code, no new dependency, no prompt, no model/provider change. The cost is dominated by reading, not writing: the plan's §7.1/§8 anchors were largely stale and every one of them had to be re-pinned against the tree before it could be encoded.
risk:
The dominant risk is a source-grep gate silently becoming a source-grep TEST. AGENTS.md bans source-grep from tests in absolute terms, and four of the eleven gates are `grep -rn` counts. The natural-looking move — 'make the gates CI-enforced' — lands them in a `*.test.ts` and violates the rule while appearing to strengthen the milestone. The gates stay a reviewer-run script; CI enforcement would need a different mechanism (a lint rule or oxlint rule, which AGENTS.md explicitly names as the correct home for structural invariants).

Second risk, and the one that costs the most: encoding a stale anchor. Thirteen of the plan's line references in these two sections are wrong, several of them only slightly (ui-helpers.ts:141 is really 143, settings.ts:108 is really 110), so a reviewer skimming will not catch them. Three of them are worse than off-by-a-few — `loader.ts:107` names `packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts` while a DIFFERENT `loader.ts` lives at `packages/tui/src/theme/loader.ts` and the §7.1/§8.2 discussion interleaves the two; a grep in the wrong loader.ts silently matches nothing.

Third risk, procedural: §7.2's four human judgements and §8.6's five human sign-offs are the parts a script cannot do, and they are the parts that would be easiest to tick off once a script exists and prints green. The doc must keep them visibly OPEN. A green gate run is evidence that eleven mechanical properties hold; it is not evidence that the work was lawful or that the UI feels right, and the sign-off grid must not blur those.
open_questions: §8.6 #5 (HUMAN, blocks step 1): does the clean-room policy get written as a docs/ file, a CONTRIBUTING.md addendum, or both? The plan weighs both and decides neither. This is a five-minute answer from the maintainer and it changes one file in this spec's `files_touched`.

§8.6 #1 (HUMAN, not resolvable in-repo): has anyone read Anthropic's current Commercial Terms on reverse engineering, derivative works and UI simulation? The plan is explicit that the researcher did NOT. The line 'All rights to Claude Code belong to Anthropic' is CCB's self-representation, not a verified reading of upstream terms. Until answered, the doc's sign-off grid shows this OPEN and asserts no clean-room status.

§8.6 #4 (HUMAN): should out-of-lock code be forced to declare itself so it can reach the notices file? This turned out to be a different question than the plan frames it — see plan_corrections. Needs a decision on whether a hand-maintained manifest is added, or whether the clean-room rule alone is sufficient.

GATE OWNERSHIP: should the gate script be wired into CI at all, or stay a reviewer-run script? This spec keeps it reviewer-run because CI enforcement of a source grep is the AGENTS.md-banned shape. If CI enforcement is wanted, the right home is an oxlint rule for the structural invariants and a real test for the behavioural ones — a different work item.

SCOPE: is tail1 part of milestone 3's definition of done, or a separate close-out? It is not one of the six waves. If it is close-out, it runs once at the end and several gates stay permanently red (G6 if A2/D1 was descoped); if it is a gate on every wave, the red-before property must be preserved per wave rather than once.
